# Waypoint's invariants

The promises in `AGENTS.md`'s "Waypoint's promises", numbered, each with the checks that already hold it. The second review checks every one a risky pull request touches: a positive and a negative test per invariant touched, and any weakening of a check named here is blocking unless the linked issue asked for it. The full wording, with every exception, is in `AGENTS.md`; this list names the checks.

1. **Email stays on the server.** A message is read in memory for its booking; what is stored is the booking's fields, its Gmail id and, while something needs it, its subject, sender's domain and day, capped text and allowlisted markup, encrypted with `WAYPOINT_SECRET_KEY` (`storage/stored_mail.py`), deleted with its item, booking or mailbox. The scan's summary and every log line are counts, never a subject, sender or text. Held by: `tests/privacy.py`'s `no_leaks` around every test that reads mail (canary values in the body, the image bytes and the image addresses), `tests/test_hostile_markup.py` and `frontend/src/lib/email-render.test.ts` (the corpus in `tests/hostile_markup.py` comes out of the cleaner and the inline renderer inert), `tests/test_review_push.py` (a push after a scan carries counts only), Semgrep's `waypoint-mail-image-fetch` (image downloads only in `providers/mailimages.py`), the Semgrep rules that keep a message's body (`payload`, `raw`, decoded parts) in `domain/mail/extract.py` and decrypting in the storage layer, and Google's hosts only in `providers/gmail.py`.
2. **Email reaches an AI only when the household chose it.** The household chose it by saving an Ollama address in Settings → AI; there is no mode, no hosted provider (OpenRouter was removed), no key and no second setting, and an empty address means no AI (owner decisions of 2026-11-17, issue #811: "use AI whenever a booking email has gaps, no additional toggle" and "kill OpenRouter support, force local AI, no option to disable AI: leave the Ollama address empty to not use AI"). Mail code gets its AI config only from `ai.mail_config`, which is `None` until an address and model are saved, and `ai.suggest` is called only by `scan._read`; the text goes unredacted to that server alone; an assistant over `/mcp` gets a message's text only on a connection granted the `mail` scope. Held by: Semgrep's `waypoint-ai-hosts`, `waypoint-ai-suggest-caller`, `waypoint-ai-suggest-caller-in-scan` and `waypoint-ai-suggest-import`, `tests/test_mail_ai.py` (`ConfiguredAddressTests`: with no address nothing reaches any AI host), `tests/test_mail_ai_auto.py` (`SavedAddressTests`: a scan asks only while an address is saved), `tests/test_migrations.py` and `tests/test_backup.py` (an old mode, hosted key or switched-off address never starts sending after an upgrade or a restore), `tests/test_mail_ai_dismiss.py` (an AI verdict, error, timeout or unreadable answer leaves the Review item and its stored message in place, for Ask AI and for a scan; only a person dismissing the item deletes mail), `tests/test_trip_destination.py` (the destination prompt is redacted of codes, names, addresses and numbers), and `tests/test_mcp_routes.py` and `tests/test_mcp_review.py` (the two routes that return email text need `mail`; without it an item is its parsed fields only).
3. **A kept message and its images are shown only to those who can see its item or booking.** The message and image routes, `GET /api/segments/{id}/code` (a parking booking's gate code, sealed in `segment_codes`) and `GET /api/offline` answer 404 to anyone else and are blocked for assistants; the offline copy holds no images, and no gate code except in the iPhone app's copy: for a request made with the app's token only, the picture of the not cancelled parking bookings the requester can see on the trips saved for them, stored protected on the phone with the saved trips and deleted with them (owner decision, #819, 2026-11-18); a browser session's reply carries none. Held by: `tests/test_offline.py` (canary values in `GET /api/offline`), `tests/test_gate_codes.py` (rule, follow-up, sealing, backup, deletion, visibility, `/mcp`, canaries), `tests/test_mcp_routes.py`, and `tests/test_every_route.py` (every route needs sign-in).
4. **You see the trips you're on.** A trip is visible to its people (everyone named on any of its bookings), to whoever booked it or one of its bookings, and to whoever got a confirmation for one in their own mailbox; nobody else, by any route, and a trip or segment you can't see is a 404, the same as one that doesn't exist. Held by: Semgrep's `waypoint-trip-visibility` (no trip or segment query in `waypoint/server/` outside `domain/visibility.py`), `tests/test_trip_people.py` (a trip's people include everyone on its bookings), each route's 404 test for a trip you can't see, and a booking's point read from disk and a stranger's 404 for a trip's places (`tests/test_geocode.py`, `tests/test_trips.py`). A trip's coordinates go to an outside service only through Apple's MapKit, for three maps (apart from the iPhone app's address lookup, which sends the text of one booking's address and no coordinate, trip or other stop: the booking's address text goes from the phone to Apple's geocoder, only while location is allowed and never with the phone's location (owner decision 3 on #819, 2026-11-18; held by `ArrivalPlacesTests`' `testNothingIsLookedUpWithoutLocationPermission`, `testNothingMoreIsSentToAppleOnceLocationIsRevokedMidBatch` and `testOnlyParkingCarPickupsAndHotelsQualify`, and `tests/test_ios_arrival_privacy.py`; the phone's location is used on the phone only, by region monitoring and a local notification that names the kind only, never sent or logged, and the arrival file holds only each watched booking's id, trip id, kind, window, circle centre and radius and when its alert last fired (no track of where the person was and no record of an arrival beyond that alert time; owner decision, issue #849 comment, 2026-11-18), dropped when its window ends and deleted by every purge: `ArrivalWatchTests`, `ArrivalPrivacyTests` and `tests/test_ios_arrival_privacy.py`)): the route replay's and the Stats map, when a MapKit key is configured on the server and `WAYPOINT_MAPKIT_ENABLED` has not been turned off (on by default, inactive without a key; the Content-Security-Policy is widened only while it is active: `https://*.apple-mapkit.com` and `blob:` in `img-src`, `connect-src` and `worker-src`, and `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` in `script-src`; the owner's decision on issue #530, with no household setting or per-trip exclusion). Then Apple's script is loaded from Apple's servers on every signed-in app open (in the background when the browser is idle, a few seconds after load, whether or not a map is shown; the owner's decision on issue #759, 2026-11-16: asked whether MapKit could "always have this loaded in the background" and told that Apple would then see the viewer's IP and this Waypoint's address on every signed-in open, the owner chose "Preload when idle after sign-in"; never offline, in the static demo or when the server reports no MapKit), is not pinned (it is Apple's auto-updating address, `https://cdn.apple-mapkit.com/mk/x/mapkit.js`, which Apple changes and browsers cache for minutes, so no integrity hash is possible) and runs in the page with the app's own access (the signed-in session's same-origin API, the trips and loyalty numbers on screen, the offline copy), so with MapKit active you are trusting Apple, not only sending it a viewport; Apple also learns the viewer's IP address and browser, and that this Waypoint's address was the page's origin (the script's request carries it as `Origin`, and the server-signed token MapKit is started with carries the Team ID), on every signed-in app open, and from a drawn map the area on screen, and, from a Past trips list, the signed snapshot address's centre and zoom (no closer than city level; a road trip's area includes Home; a very wide trip gets a 640 px zoom-3 image centred on the route, clipped) and size for each card with no photos and two or more stops (`GET /api/map-snapshots`: sign-in required, blocked for assistants, a trip you can't see left out, the server only signs and never fetches the image, no card asks when photo coverage is unknown; `tests/test_map_snapshots.py`), and the exact start and end coordinates of each drive in the replay (a car leg, Home included; never a flight, cruise or train), which the browser sends to Apple's directions service to trace the route along roads (a failed call keeps a straight line; the owner's decision, issue #630); the one thing the server sends Apple is the background job that prepares past trips' driving roads ahead of time once a night at midnight server time, never at startup, while a key is active (the owner's decisions on issue #829, 2026-11-18): Apple's Maps Server API (`maps-api.apple.com`, `providers/mapkit.py` only) gets one drive's exact start and end coordinates at a time, only for a drive the replay would draw that has no stored road, writing only the trip's stored roads and adding no read path of its own (the roads it prepares then feed the trip's distance in the summary), stopping on 401 or 403, logging counts only (`tests/test_route_warming.py`; Semgrep's `waypoint-apple-maps-server-host`, which keeps the host in `providers/mapkit.py`, and `waypoint-apple-directions-caller`, which lets only `domain/route_warming.py` call `mapkit.Directions` or import the module under another name; and the shared fixture `tests/fixtures/route_stops.json`, asserted by both `tests/test_route_warming.py` and `frontend/src/lib/route-replay.test.ts`, which ties the server's choice of drives to the replay's `stopsOf`, `isDrive` and `worthLocating`); the server otherwise only signs a short-lived token (`GET /api/mapkit/token`, sign-in required, blocked for assistants, the private key never returned or logged, the Key ID and Team ID never logged; the token itself carries them as `kid` and `iss`). With no key or the flag off nothing goes to Apple, the Content-Security-Policy names no Apple host and the replay is not shown and a Past trips card shows its kinds tile; a MapKit failure before it showed hides it, and one after it showed replaces it with the line "The map couldn’t load". On a completed trip's page the desktop column's still Apple map is drawn as the page opens, so its area and the drives with no stored road reach Apple then, not only when Replay trip is pressed. The Stats map is Apple's too (the owner's decisions on #828 and #833, 2026-11-18): opening Stats with a key draws one live map of the chosen period's travel, so Apple learns the area on screen and every area the viewer pans or zooms to, and Apple's script is handed only geometry and style (the positions of the period's airports, flight arcs and stay pins and the outlines of the visited countries and US states; never a name, count, date or trip) to draw (the outlines are bundled with the app and loaded from this Waypoint, never fetched from Apple and not loaded with no key; with no key Stats has no map and a failed MapKit collapses the slot). Picking a mark to list its trips is pointer-only (the owner's decision on #838, 2026-11-18: keyboard picking of map marks is dropped). The one map not drawn by Apple is the Year in Review card image, drawn on the device from the bundled outlines because it becomes a downloadable image and Apple's terms don't clearly allow Apple imagery in one (the owner's decision on #838, 2026-11-18); it never contacts Apple. Held by: Semgrep's `waypoint-no-bundled-map` and `waypoint-no-bundled-map-outlines`, `StatsMapKit.svelte.test.ts` and `Stats.svelte.test.ts`, `tests/test_mapkit.py`, Semgrep's `waypoint-driving-route-rows` (stored roads are queried only in `domain/driving_routes.py`, which the trip summary's distance reads through, and `domain/route_warming.py`), `tests/test_trip_summary.py` (another trip's road for the same drive is never counted), the MapKit Vitest suites (`RouteReplay.svelte.test.ts`, `RouteReplayHidden.svelte.test.ts`, `RouteReplayMapKit.svelte.test.ts`, including `App.svelte.test.ts`'s "preloading MapKit") and Semgrep's `waypoint-mapkit-hosts`, `tests/test_map_snapshots.py` and the Past trips card suites (`RouteTile.svelte.test.ts`, `PastTripCard.svelte.test.ts`, `Trips.svelte.test.ts`).
5. **IDs are for the household.** Loyalty and Known Traveler numbers are visible to every signed-in member, encrypted at rest, masked until asked for, and never in logs, reports, notifications, hosted AI prompts or the browser's storage (the device's encrypted offline copy excepted, which never holds one). Held by: Semgrep (decrypting only in the storage layer, `oidc.py`, `domain/loyalty.py` and `providers/gmail.py`), ESLint (nothing kept in the browser's storage; the Cache API only in `frontend/src/lib/offline-vault.ts`), `tests/test_offline.py` (canary numbers never in `GET /api/offline`), `tests/test_loyalty.py`, and `no_leaks` in the tests.
6. **Times are where they happen.** A booking's times are wall-clock times at its airports or hotel, stored with the place's IANA zone; nothing converts them to the server's zone or UTC on the way; "today" and scheduled hours are the machine's local time, and anything that tells another system about a time carries the right zone. Held by: Semgrep (no naive `datetime.now()` in domain or provider code, no bare `date.today()` in background jobs and provider modules, no `datetime.utcnow()`; month arithmetic only in `waypoint/dates.py`), strict mypy over `domain/` and `providers/`, and `tests/test_dates.py`.
7. **Every route is held without a test of its own.** A new route needs sign-in, refuses a change without the app's header or from another site, has its reply typed in `waypoint/server/contract.py` and has a docs page. Held by: `tests/test_every_route.py`, `make api-contract-check` and `make feature-map-check` (every route has a test: `tools/feature_map_allowlist.txt` started empty and stays that way).
8. **Access ends with the person.** Every kind of session, grant, token, feed key or mailbox connection ends when its owner can no longer sign in, like browser sessions do. Held by: `oidc.access_lapsed`, and each kind's own test: `tests/test_hardening.py` (`test_removed_email_ends_sessions`), `tests/test_gmail.py` (a lapsed owner's mailbox connection is ended by the sweep, by listing mailboxes and even when Google can't be told), `tests/test_mcp_oauth.py` and `tests/test_mcp_oauth_http.py` (assistant connections), and `tests/test_reminders.py`. A new kind of credential needs a test like these; none of them covers it by itself.
9. **Nothing about the app leaves it.** Waypoint sends nothing about itself to any outside service (the iPhone app's address lookup and the MapKit case, both in invariant 4: the MapKit case is Apple's unpinned script and map images running in the viewer's page, which also draws the Stats map, plus the one background job there that asks Apple's Maps Server API for a drive's roads): no telemetry, error reporting or analytics SDKs, every log line through `monitoring.log`, and every outbound connection through `tls.urlopen` (or `tls.post_http2` for Apple's HTTP/2 push). Held by: Semgrep's `waypoint-no-telemetry` and the `tls.urlopen` and `waypoint-raw-httpx` paved-path rules, ESLint (no `console.log`; `fetch(` only in `lib/api.ts`), and `no_leaks` (a canary in a request sent through `tls.urlopen` or `tls.post_http2` fails).
10. **Backups restore what was there.** A backup holds the encrypted message text and gate codes as they were, and `backup.restore` refuses one made at an older schema revision than the baseline with a message saying so. Held by: `tests/test_backup.py` and `tests/test_gate_codes.py`.
11. **The automation is checked the way the code is.** Workflows run bash with `-eo pipefail`, pin every action by SHA with its version in a comment, check out with `persist-credentials: false`, pass event values as environment variables, paginate `gh api` lists, and run on `vars.RUNS_ON` or say why they stay on GitHub's runners; the reviews and the merge gate run from main's copies, and the fleet workflows are pinned by commit at one version. Held by: the fleet checks' workflow conventions, zizmor in the security scans, and fleet's `sync.yml` (pins that disagree fail).
12. **Photos are shared by their person.** A photo reaches someone else only while its person's grant for that trip is active with the Trip scope, the viewer is one of the trip's people, and it is not excluded; every trip-facing reply, count, pin and image is built from the photos that one predicate (`photos.visible`) lets the viewer see, assistants included, and taking a photo back takes effect on the next request. The two intentional exceptions are person-only: Needs a look and its image routes use `photos.unsettled`, and the removed-photo thumbnail uses `photos.removed`. AGENTS.md "Photos are shared by their person" has the full text (cache headers, stream cut-off on removal, the Immich address and key never reaching the browser, the same 404 for every refusal). Held by: Semgrep's `waypoint-photo-access` (no `Photo` query or insert in `waypoint/server/`, `waypoint/domain/` or `waypoint/storage/` outside `photos.py`, `photogrants.py` and `photosync.py`; `storage/models.py` and `storage/photo_sources.py` are scanned, the table mapping and the source counts carry a line-level `nosemgrep`, and so do the demo seed rows in `domain/demo.py`), `tests/test_photo_access.py`, `tests/test_photo_proxy.py` and `no_leaks` with canary asset ids and places.
